guide.title: Proposed: Style Guide V2.10, a dry corporate snark

rules.text: Dummy Corporation: deadpan and inspirational, with a dry corporate snark. The trainee is an asset under review: a flat, procedural put-down, then the instruction. No cheer, no "!", no wink, no insult to the body's pain (T4 holds).
Feedback (a miss, a denial, a held chassis, NOT COUNTED): a put-down of at most three words, then what to do, in the imperative. At most 60 characters, to fit the strip.
Status lines (COUNTED, TILE CLEARED, combo tallies, drone captions) stay crisp. Praise is withheld, not given. At most one put-down in three.
Unchanged. Their tier voices already carry the snark (T6 to T12).

guide.note: Your example set the direction: "Try harder - bait a car to divert and get hit." V2.9 (T1) counted sarcasm as a fault; V2.10 lets the Corporation be dry. Approve it and the new lines follow it; keep V2.9 and they are judged by the old rule.
